newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African wool prices fall at latest auction.
newsitem.headline: South African wool prices fall at latest auction.

text.p: South African wool prices were lower at the season's weekly auction, the Wool Board said on Thursday.
It said 10,716 bales were offered at this week's sale, of which 94.6 percent was sold.

Price quotes for long Merino fleeces of 20 micron shed 8.7 percent to 25.17 rand/kg, 21 micron dropped 7.1 percent to 22.63 rand/kg, 22 micron fell 2.9 percent to 20.18 rand/kg, 23 micron declined 0.7 percent to 18.13 rand/kg, 24 micron dipped 0.2 percent to 17.27 rand/kg and 25 micron dropped 0.3 percent to 16.83 rand/kg.
Prices for Merino bellies gained 0.9 percent to 18.24 rand/kg, Merino lambs dropped five percent to 23.28 rand/kg and Merino locks fell 1.4 percent to 13.75 rand/kg.

The board noted that the Australian market had declined sharply for the second consecutive week. According to analysts, the large volumes of wool presently being offered at auction impacted negatively on the market since demand was not strong enough to sustain price levels.
